design: The design record is README.md (operating doc), PLAN.md (reasoning, vendor column mapping) and dashboard/COHORT_TOOL.md (cohort API and page). AGENTS.md holds the rules. A change that contradicts any of them must say so in its spec and update the doc in the same PR. This repo is public and the data is patient data: specs, commits and PR text use synthetic examples and column names, never real counts, values or identifiers.
seamNote: deid.py (PHI column lists, id hashing, date shift, leak assert), config.connect(), db.bulk_insert, sql/unified.sql, the cohort API's suppression and allow-lists, the MCP query guard

spec.design: files to add/change under src/uccc_genomics/, mcp/, dashboard/ or systemd/; functions and their signatures; schema.table and column names for any data change, with the vendor source field each comes from (PLAN.md mapping); for anything that leaves the de-id file (dashboard loader, cohort API, MCP tool), the small-cell rule it applies and how; whether research_id or report_id stability is affected (it must not be). The test plan uses synthetic Caris JSON / FMI XML / DuckDB built in the test under a temp DATA dir, never $DATA/raw or the PHI file

implement: Run `uv sync --all-packages` first in a fresh worktree (plain `uv sync` misses the mcp/ member). Tests build synthetic inputs in temp dirs (see tests/test_pipeline.py); never read $DATA/raw/ or genomics_phi.duckdb, and never write to the real $DATA. Never run `genomics sync|load|deid|all` against the real $DATA, `npm run deploy`, `wrangler deploy`, or systemctl on the services; never touch the key files. Stop any dev server you start. Report the dashboard check as n/a when the change cannot affect dashboard/.

checks.name: dashboard
checks.command: cd dashboard && npm ci && npm test

lenses.code: CODE review. Correctness against the issue spec and its acceptance criteria; tests that would actually catch a regression (synthetic fixtures in temp dirs, no network, never $DATA/raw or the PHI file); loads stay full drop-and-rebuild from the raw mirror; vendor quirks in README/PLAN.md are preserved (Caris newest-JSON-wins, FMI Monitor files, FMI missing MRN, fmi.load_error so nothing drops silently); new disease terms go in disease_crosswalk.csv, not SQL special cases; unified.* stays UNION ALL BY NAME with a vendor column; bulk loads go through db.bulk_insert; dependency choices against AGENTS.md (uv, stdlib, polars not pandas, no new deps without reason); dead code. The spec and the code must agree: a stale spec is "major", because later issues copy it.
lenses.security: PRIVACY + SECURITY review. No PHI reaches the de-id file, logs, fixtures, commits, specs or PR text: check deid.py's drop lists and leak assert against any new column, not just the tests. research_id/report_id stay keyed hashes, stable for the same key; dates stay shifted per patient; ages capped at 89. Every path out of the de-id file (dashboard loader, cohort API, MCP tool) floors counts under 5, emits no row-level ids, and the cohort API keeps secondary suppression, the whole-cohort rule, allow-listed parameters and bound SQL only. The MCP connection keeps enable_external_access=false, lock_configuration=true and the row cap. The cohort API refuses requests without a valid Access JWT (only /api/health open); wrangler.toml keeps workers_dev and previews off. No keys, .env values, bucket or host names in code or docs.
lenses.ux: UX review for clinicians and researchers on the dashboard and agents using the MCP server. Dashboard: labels and legends say what is counted (patients vs reports, which vendors), suppressed cells are shown as suppressed not zero, filters and shareable query-string links work, readable on mobile and in light/dark mode, accessibility (contrast, headings, keyboard focus). MCP tools and cohort API: names and descriptions say what they answer, errors name the bad parameter, results are small. README and AGENTS.md stay accurate for a first-time user.
